summary: Edge proxy connection stall from slow chunked uploads and header growth causing delayed TTFB for long completions
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC, Acme Payments reported intermittent large increases in TTFB (time-to-first-byte) for streaming completions >60s. The pattern is correlated with clients that upload request bodies slowly (chunked transfer) while also sending periodic trace/authorization header updates. Impact: Customer-facing inference calls return with long stalls before streaming begins; some requests trigger ALB/edge connection resets and 504s. Environment: prod-us-east-1, traffic through our public API Gateway -> edge proxy layer -> internal ALB -> serving runtime. Observed behavior: When the client uploads body slowly (multi-second pauses between chunks) and repeatedly sends header updates, the edge proxy's HPACK table grows and proxy buffering increases, triggering idle-send-timeouts or partial flush behavior. Expected behavior: Streaming should begin when the server has the initial request payload and upstream should not stall due to header accumulation or slow chunked uploads. Additional notes: This looks related to previous header-growth/idle-timeout tickets but differs because root trigger is slow-client upload combined with periodic header rotation (trace IDs/authorization refresh) that causes HPACK and proxy state churn.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client that sends a chunked POST to /v1/chat/stream with a ~1.5MB prompt encoded in many small chunks (200-500B) with 200-500ms pauses between chunks.
2) Configure the client to rotate a custom 'x-trace' header every 5s while upload is in progress to simulate streaming telemetry/refreshing tokens.
3) Observe the edge proxy connection and ALB during the upload and the downstream serving runtime's TTFB for the completion stream.
4) Compare with a single non-chunked upload of the same payload (should start streaming immediately).

comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Sharma (Support): Customer reports ~30-60s stalls before we emit the first streaming token. Happens multiple times per hour. Provided curl script and pcap.

2026-03-10 Diego Martinez (SRE): Reproduced locally with synthetic client. Confirmed TTFB delay correlates with slow chunked upload and repeated header updates. Suspect HPACK table growth plus proxy buffering logic interacting with ALB idle-send-timeout.

2026-03-11 Mara Lee (Runtime): Serving runtime shows requests not starting generate loop until full body seen; however we should be able to start streaming earlier for long-completion paths. Investigating whether proxy signals 'client body not complete' semantics upstream.

2026-03-11 Support (to customer): Recommended temporary workaround: disable header rotation during upload, or send the prompt as a single upload (non-chunked) when possible. Customer testing confirmed immediate improvement.

2026-03-12 Diego Martinez (SRE): Edge proxy team pushed a configuration flag to reduce HPACK table max and lower proxy buffer threshold in canary proxies in us-east-1 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1294). Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-12 Acme Payments (customer): Confirmed reduction in TTFB spikes on the canary route; filing follow-up to consider long-term fix for header parsing backpressure.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Large header growth causes the proxy to delay flushes and then ALB considers connection idle leading to resets.
Packet captures show client pauses of 200-500ms between content chunks; edge proxy continues to accept but defers streaming to upstream until client body completeness flag is set.
HPACK growth observed because header rotation sends slightly different header values frequently (x-trace, x-client-info), causing table churn and increased memory used by header tables.
ALB/edge idle-send-timeout is 30s; combined slow upload + multiple small back-and-forths increases end-to-end time before initial server response and can cross that timeout window for some requests.
Temporarily lowering HPACK table size and enabling earlier flush path in canary has reduced reproductions from 8/10 to 1/10 in initial runs.

Potential long-term fixes: 1) treat chunked request body reads as enough to begin upstream streaming once a minimal prefix is received; 2) add heuristics to ignore frequent small header changes during an active body upload; 3) tune ALB/edge idle timeouts per route.
resolution: Workaround applied and validated: canary proxies in us-east-1 rolled with reduced HPACK table size and lowered proxy buffering threshold (rolled 2026-03-12). Customer asked to avoid rotating auth/trace headers during uploads; they implemented this and reported improvement. Next steps: engineering to evaluate upstream change to start streaming on partial body availability (RFC), and product discussion on adjusting default idle-send-timeouts for streaming endpoints. Postmortem and permanent fix planned; keeping ticket open until runtime change or config-managed mitigation is deployed globally.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to draft RFC for partial-body streaming behavior (owner: Mara Lee) - target 2026-03-19
2) Edge team to run extended canary for 48h and collect TTFB metrics across clusters (owner: Diego Martinez) - target 2026-03-14
